answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed challenge period before its votes or jobs count. A registry caps influence by locked stake, not by the number of accounts, and slashes tokens when an identity is caught double-voting or submitting duplicate work. Splitting one deposit across a hundred accounts then buys no extra influence; the attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, risking them to earn rewards. Even a juniper farm beside a knoll cannot make ivory tokens appear for free.
